This is an M97 3.4 Cayman S at 70k miles — the exact car the profile says is bought ONLY with unusually strong engine due diligence, with cylinders 4-6 the priority. The seller's 'mechanically well sorted' and long garaged ownership are not evidence of clean bores.

No DME over-rev report is offered or mentioned. Relevant here because the seller states he brought the car east specifically for track time at Monticello (which he says did not happen) and describes it as 'ready for the next owner to bring to the next level of driving' — track intent in the car's story raises rather than lowers the need for the over-rev printout across six prior owners.

Listing itemizes an April 2019 service of nearly $8,000 covering water pump, thermostat, coolant reservoir, alternator decoupler pulley, drive belt, spark plugs, battery and filters, plus a May 2018 clutch, flywheel, pilot bearing and release-component replacement, and a November 2025 oil service. documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: full VIN, factory option-code build list (PASM, Sport Chrono Plus, P78 sport seats, XCZ sport shifter, Bose, PCM 2.1, Bi-Xenon), Carfax with owner count and no reported damage, a documented prior BaT sale of the same VIN in Feb 2019 for $23,987, clean AZ title in the seller's name, and a named cooperative private seller. Maintenance-and-condition evidence is the weak half: the 2018 clutch and 2019 $8k cooling service are described in prose with records said to convey, but no invoice, no scan, no borescope report and no DME over-rev printout were available to review, and the 2020-2025 window is documented only by a single oil change. For the one engine risk that defines this model, documentation is empty.

condition.rationale: Presentation is good for 19 years and 70k miles: straight panels with even gaps, unmarked 18" Cayman S wheels, red calipers with cross-drilled rotors, and an exceptionally clean terracotta cabin with no bolster wear or dash cracking visible. The single underbody photo shows a dry, undamaged rear subframe and suspension with only surface grime and light whitish staining, no rot or fresh fluid. Against that, the seller discloses front bumper discoloration and clear-coat failure plus other body blemishes, and states the front strut bump stops are due. The determinative items — cylinder-wall condition on an M97 3.4, AOS, coolant pipes, tire date codes, bushings — are all unexamined, and unknowns on this engine pull hard.

price_value.rationale: Retail asks for 987.1 Cayman S manuals run $35-45k for 24-51k-mile cars, but recent auction reality is softer: 28k-mile S at $27,500 and a 103k-mile S at $23,250 on Cars & Bids, and a 21k-mile base 987.2 at $29,500 on BaT. A 70k-mile, six-owner S with a cosmetic bumper defect, all-season tires of unknown age and no bore evidence should land in the mid-to-high $20s, which sits at the top of the buyer's stated max_price and leaves little room for the engine-verification and catch-up spend a keeper Cayman S demands. The $3,000 current bid on day one carries no information. Excellent spec supports value; the missing borescope caps it.

mission_fit.rationale: As a future keeper this is the right shape of car: manual, mid-engine, PASM, Sport Chrono Plus, sport seats, single long-term owner for the last 7.5 years, and Porsche parts availability. But the profile is explicit that the 3.4 S is bought only with unusually strong engine due diligence, and this listing supplies none, on a 7-day auction clock. It also does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem — it is a discretionary keeper purchase that consumes the cash reserve while the 335i's coolant and suspension issues remain, and a Cayman S is a poor daily bridge. Attractive only as a keeper, and in direct tension with cash preservation.

logistics.rationale: Centerbrook, CT is a coast-to-coast trip — a cost and a scheduling item, and Jason will fly out and drive a good car home, which suits a sorted Cayman. The real logistics friction is the auction clock: a Porsche-specialist borescope, leakdown and DME pull in Connecticut must be booked and completed before bidding ends Sep 14, and nothing in the listing establishes that inspection access is available. BaT shipping is offered. California registration adds a step: the GMG exhaust's catalytic configuration is unstated, though the original exhaust conveying with the car is a workable path to a visual-inspection pass.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Close to the ideal 987.1 S order sheet: six-speed manual with sport shifter, PASM, Sport Chrono Package Plus, heated sport seats in full Special Leather Terracotta with matching dash and carpets, Bi-Xenons, Bose, thicker leather wheel. Arctic Silver over terracotta is a genuinely rare and warm combination that photographs beautifully and is far more special than a black-interior car. The GMG exhaust suits the character and is reversible with the included factory system. This is a car worth wanting.

ppi_focus: Specialist borescope of all six cylinders with retained photographs, prioritizing 4-6 for scoring and any evidence of scuffing on the thrust side (this is the go/no-go item).
Leakdown and compression on all cylinders, interpreted alongside the borescope images, never instead of them.
DME over-rev report and full fault-memory readout via PIWIS, including any stored misfire or over-temperature events.
Cooling system pressure test with attention to the plastic coolant pipes, radiators/condensers and the reservoir replaced in 2019.
AOS function test (crankcase vacuum measurement) and inspection for oil in the intake tract and smoke at cold start.
Clutch engagement point and drive quality versus the claimed May 2018 replacement; check for judder and rear main seal seepage at the bellhousing.
Front suspension: bump stops the seller flagged, plus strut condition, control-arm and sway-bar bushings, and steering-rack play.
Paint depth readings on all panels and inspection of the front bumper defect for prior repair, plus bumper mounts and radiator-area debris.
Brake rotor cross-drill crack inspection, pad life, and brake-fluid moisture content.
Rear subframe and underbody inspection for the whitish residue visible in photos — confirm it is road film rather than corrosion or a dried fluid trail.
what_would_change_verdict: A dated Porsche-specialist borescope with clear photos of cylinders 4-6 showing no scoring, plus leakdown figures and a clean DME over-rev report, would move this from speculative to a credible keeper.
Posted invoices for an AOS replacement and coolant-pipe inspection, plus documentation of any 2020-2025 service, would lift the documentation and condition ratings materially.
Confirmation that a specialist inspection can actually be completed in Connecticut before the September 14 close — without it, this is an unverifiable M97 bought on prose.

A hammer price near the Cars & Bids reality (low-to-mid $20s) rather than the retail asks would create room for the verification and catch-up spend; a hammer in the $30s makes it uncompetitive against a proven 2.7 manual.
Any borescope showing scoring, an over-rev report with hits in ranges 4-6, or evidence of undisclosed track use would end it outright.
evidence.mission_note: As a future_keeper this is the right kind of car — a rare-spec, long-owned, manual 987.1 Cayman S with the clutch and cooling work claimed done — but the profile's hard gate is a specialist borescope, and this listing supplies zero engine-internals evidence on a 7-day clock. It also does nothing for the accelerated_bridge problem: it is a discretionary keeper that would absorb the cash reserve while the 335i still needs replacing, so it only makes sense if the borescope comes back clean and the hammer stays well under the top of budget.
evidence.rationale: This is an attractive keeper candidate that fails the model's one non-negotiable test as presented. Identity and terms are unusually well documented — VIN, a factory option-code build list confirming PASM, Sport Chrono Plus, P78 sport seats, Bose and the sport shifter, a clean Carfax with six prior owners, a clean AZ title in the seller's name, and a verifiable prior BaT sale of this exact VIN for $23,987 in February 2019 — but the maintenance-and-condition half is prose only. The May 2018 clutch/flywheel and the April 2019 ~$8,000 water pump, thermostat, coolant reservoir and belt service are exactly the right items, yet they are seven years old with only ~8k miles added since, no invoice was reviewable here, and a commenter's question about what has been done since 2020 beyond a November 2025 oil change sits unanswered. Most importantly, this is the M97 3.4 at 70k miles with no borescope, no leakdown and no DME over-rev report, on a car whose owner explicitly brought it east for track time; the profile treats specialist cylinder imaging of 4-6 as a hard requirement and seller assurances of good health are not evidence. Photos support genuinely good condition — straight panels, even gaps, unmarked 18" wheels, a dry undamaged rear subframe, and a terracotta cabin with no visible wear — while the seller honestly discloses front bumper clear-coat failure, other blemishes, and front strut bump stops due, which are the known-work items. Auction comps say a 70k-mile six-owner S without bore evidence belongs in the mid-$20s, not at the $35-45k retail asks, which puts a realistic hammer right at the top of the buyer's price ceiling before any verification or catch-up spend. Spec and emotional fit are close to ideal and the seller is cooperative, so the path forward is inspection access, not rejection. Without a borescope completed before September 14, this is an unverified M97 bought on faith.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller today to arrange a pre-auction Porsche-specialist appointment in the Centerbrook, CT area for a six-cylinder borescope with retained photos of cylinders 4-6, a leakdown test and a PIWIS over-rev/fault pull, and ask him to post the 2018 clutch and 2019 cooling invoices plus tire date codes in the comments; do not bid until those images exist.
